hero.eyebrow: A research desk for everything you save
hero.sub: Save anything worth reading. The Lede reads it closely, unburies the real story, files it by beat, and writes the strongest honest case the piece can make. Your queue becomes a magazine, not a pile of tabs.

signup.topEyebrow: Coming to iPhone · one email when it opens
signup.closingSub: No account, ever. Your library lives in your own iCloud, and your first ten briefs each month are free.
signup.disclaimer: One email, when it opens. Nothing else, no list-sharing. The privacy policy covers it.
signup.alertInvalid: That address didn’t look like an email. Check it and send it again.
signup.alertError: Something broke on our end and your address wasn’t saved. Please try again in a minute.

showcase1.heading: Your saves file themselves into a magazine.
showcase1.body: Every story comes back renamed for what it’s actually about and shelved on its beat. The queue reads like sections you pick by mood.

showcase2.heading: The strongest honest case, before you commit to the read.
showcase2.body: Every save comes back as a short brief: the fairest version of the argument, enough to know what you’re dealing with. When something matters, send The Lede out to dig deeper: more reporting, other angles, an honest bottom line. It works the same on a news story, a how-to, or the history thread you fell into at midnight.
showcase2.featureHeading: It finds the reporting under the opinion.
showcase2.featureBody: The Lede reads every source as it is. It doesn't rank outlets and it reads every one. The one thing it changes: when a piece is opinion, it builds the brief from the original reporting underneath, and shows you the reporting it used. Same rule for every publication. More on how The Lede handles sources.

founderNote.quote: “I built The Lede because I got tired of headlines that bury the story, or sell one that isn’t there.”
founderNote.attribution: Charles Klein, maker of The Lede

thanks.title: You're on the list · The Lede
thanks.sub: We’ll email you once, when The Lede is on the App Store. That’s the only reason we’ll write. No noise, no list-sharing, and you can unsubscribe in one tap. The details are in the privacy policy.
thanks.muted: Know someone drowning in open tabs? Send them theledeapp.com.
